title: Microcoalescence probe log (scratch)
content:
Context:
I wanted to try a different take on request coalescing for tiny, high-frequency spikes — what I'm calling "microcoalescence" here. The idea: instead of a single global coalescing timer (e.g., 2–10ms) tuned for average burst sizes, we dynamically tune a short-window coalescer that collapses requests arriving within very small intervals (sub-5ms) but only when beneficial to throughput/cost and without degrading P99 too much. This paper-scratch is notes + local-run logs + quick conclusions.

Goals:
- Measure whether microcoalescing (0.5–4ms windows) reduces per-token cost by improving GPU utilization for tiny bursts without increasing P99 beyond acceptable thresholds (target: +<10% relative P99).
- Test interaction with KV cache priming: does aggressive microcoalescing hurt cache-locality and increase memory churn?
- Produce a simple heuristic: when to enable microcoalescer based on recent inter-arrival histogram and active model context length.

Environment / infra used:
- Cluster: dev-dedicated-a (4xA10G per node), single-node tests with local traffic generator.
- Runtime: branch microcoalesce-experiment (commit a7b2f9) compiled with continuous-batching enabled and new coalescer module.
- Model: llama-2-mini (quantized), sequence len=128, kv-cache warm/cold toggles.
- Load generator: custom poisson+burst combiner (see linked PLT ticket).
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency (inference-only), tokens/s, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, kv-cache-hit-rate.

Experiment design (short):
1) Baseline: no microcoalescer, existing batching (dynamic up to 32), default batch timer 6ms. Run steady QPS 60, with small bursts: spikes to 250 qps for 250ms every 15s. Repeat for 30 minutes.
2) Fixed microcoalesce windows: 0.5ms, 1ms, 2ms, 4ms (coalescer collapses arrivals into a single internal request; internal dispatch still respects route priorities).
3) Adaptive microcoalescer: window starts 0.5ms and expands to 4ms if recent 100ms arrival variance is > threshold; also disabled if P95 or P99 increases above guardrail.
4) KV-cache condition toggle: primed (hot) vs cold (start-of-run invalidated) for each of above.

Key config knobs exercised:
- microcoalesce.window_ms
- microcoalesce.max_batch_contrib (how many requests coalesced counted towards batch size)
- microcoalesce-disable-if-p99-rises (guardrail boolean)
- batch.timer_ms (baseline)

Representative log excerpt (parsed):
Run: fixed-1ms, kv=hot, steady60/250spikes
- duration: 30m
- tokens/sec (avg): 12.6k
- gpu-util (avg): 62% (vs baseline 58%)
- avg batch size (inference requests): 9.4 (baseline 6.1)
- P50: 18ms (baseline 15ms)
- P95: 62ms (baseline 59ms)
- P99: 165ms (baseline 150ms)
- kv-cache-hit-rate: 94% (baseline 95%)

Run: fixed-0.5ms, kv=cold, steady60/250spikes
- tokens/sec: 11.8k
- gpu-util: 59%
- avg batch size: 7.2
- P50: 20ms
- P95: 70ms
- P99: 210ms  <-- noticeable degradation on cold cache
- kv-cache-hit-rate: 81% (cache thrash observed)

Run: adaptive, kv=hot, steady60/250spikes
- tokens/sec: 13.0k
- gpu-util: 66%
- avg batch size: 10.6
- P50: 19ms
- P95: 64ms
- P99: 158ms
- kv-cache-hit-rate: 94%

Quick interpretation:
- Microcoalescing with very small windows (0.5–1ms) increases batch size enough to gain ~7–12% tokens/sec throughput and improve GPU utilization.
- When KV cache is cold, tiny windows can increase cache churn (lower hit-rate) and cause significant P99 regressions — likely because coalesced requests mix contexts and cause unnecessary cache invalidations or memory pressure.
- The 2–4ms fixed windows give best throughput gains but start to impact P50/P95 more noticeably; 1ms is a reasonable sweet spot in hot-cache conditions.
- The adaptive approach outperformed fixed windows across mixed conditions (hot/cold) because it learns when to expand. Adaptive was able to keep P99 within our guardrail in almost all runs.

Small table (aggregated):
Configuration | tokens/sec | gpu% | avg batch | P99 (ms) | kv-hit%
baseline      | 11.5k      | 58%  | 6.1       | 150      | 95%
0.5ms-fix     | 11.8k      | 59%  | 7.2       | 210      | 81%
1ms-fix       | 12.6k      | 62%  | 9.4       | 165      | 94%
2ms-fix       | 12.9k      | 64%  | 10.1      | 178      | 93%
adaptive       | 13.0k      | 66%  | 10.6      | 158      | 94%

Edge observations (raw notes):
- At spike onset, coalescer trimmed many 1–3 request micro-bursts into single internal ops — this reduced kernel launch overhead noticeably.
- Cold KV runs: memory allocator churn showed up in p99 stacks (malloc/free during cache refill). Might be exacerbated by Python-side cache management in current test harness. Need native alloc profiling.
- Some spike patterns with very high arrival variance caused the adaptive controller to oscillate (expand then quickly collapse window). Need smoothing and hysteresis.

Quick conclusions / recommendations:
- Implement adaptive microcoalescer in runtime behind a feature flag with default disabled for dedicated/private customers.
- Default policy: enable only when model context < 256, observed inter-arrival 1ms percentile < 2ms, and kv-cache-hit-rate > 85% or when system in steady-state (not first 30s after model load).
- Add guardrails: auto-disable for 2 consecutive p99 breaches of +12% relative.
- Improve allocator/caching layering: ensure cache refills don't cause blocking allocs during coalesced dispatch.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Run longer 12h overnight stability run with adaptive mode and mixed traffic (real traces). Ticket: PLATFORM-972 assigned to me.
- [ ] Add histograms of inter-arrival time to the console dashboard for easier tuning.
- [ ] Prototype hysteresis in adaptive controller (double-window confirm before expanding/shrinking).
- [ ] Re-run cold-cache runs but with native allocator profiling (callgrind / jemalloc stats).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Might want to try combining microcoalescer with request affinity (group by session-id or kv-key fingerprint) to avoid mixing contexts.
- Consider exposing coalescer decisions as tracing spans for easier debugging in SRE/console.

If anyone reads this and wants to reproduce: check linked PR and PLT ticket. I pushed the small logging patch that records coalesced-batch ids; that helped correlate p99 spikes to coalesced batches that included requests with mismatched context-lengths.

End of scratch log.
